dedupe_keys.name: radiology workflow simulation dataset synthetic patient flows event logs exam records and resource use

description: This data set is a synthetic week of patient flows through a hospital radiology department, generated by a discrete-event simulation so that researchers can study imaging capacity without patient records. The producers are Fernando Serrano Pérez and Sergio Ilarri Artigas of the University of Zaragoza, who ran the model in the CrogMagnon simulation engine of the NEAT-AMBIENCE project and based its process on a published study of a Belgian hospital radiology department. Coverage is one medium-sized simulated department over seven days from 1 January 2023. Files give one row per patient case, per exam and per workflow event, five-minute utilisation logs for each CT, MRI, X-ray, mammography and cone-beam CT device, and metadata on arrival patterns, patient types and resource configuration, with a detailed file description. The data are available as free CSV and text downloads from Mendeley Data under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: all records are synthetic and reflect the model's assumptions, not observed demand, one week is short, and some file and column names are in Spanish. Simulation uses: benchmarking hospital queueing and scheduling methods, testing how equipment outages or demand surges lengthen waits, and training prediction of waiting times. Related records: patientflow (model-patientflow) predicts bed demand, and the SimPy healthcare models (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des) simulate hospital queues.
name: Radiology Workflow Simulation Dataset: synthetic patient flows, event logs, exam records and resource use
provider: Fernando Serrano Pérez and Sergio Ilarri Artigas (University of Zaragoza, NEAT-AMBIENCE project)
schema_summary: cases.csv (one row per simulated patient case), exams.csv (one row per exam), events.csv (one row per workflow event); resource_usage folder with 5-minute utilisation logs per imaging device (CT, MRI, X-ray, mammography, CBCT); metadata folder with arrival patterns, patient types and resource configuration; dataset_details.txt and intended_uses.txt
